holidays.name: National Coconut Cream Pie Day
holidays.description: Grab a fork and celebrate the dreamy combo of silky coconut custard, toasted coconut flakes, and a cloud of whipped cream piled into a flaky crust. It's a tropical vacation in a pie tin.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It has become a fixture on American food-holiday calendars, and pie lovers mark it every May 8.
holidays.funFact: Despite the name, a coconut cream pie is made with a custard filling. The coconut gives it flavor and texture, but the creamy base comes from milk, eggs, and cream.

holidays.name: National Have a Coke Day
holidays.description: A day to pop open a cold, fizzy cola and toast one of the most recognizable drinks on Earth. It's an excuse to share a soda with a friend.
holidays.origin: The day marks May 8, 1886. On that date in Atlanta, Georgia, pharmacist John Pemberton's new syrup drink was first sold, at Jacobs' Pharmacy.
holidays.funFact: Coca-Cola began as a medicinal tonic sold at a soda fountain. Early sales averaged only a handful of drinks per day.

holidays.name: National Give Someone a Cupcake Day
holidays.description: Today is all about spreading joy in frosted, bite-sized form. Surprise a coworker, neighbor, or stranger with a cupcake, and watch their day get better.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It is widely listed on May 8 as a day for sharing sweet treats.
holidays.funFact: Cupcakes got their name either from the cups they were baked in or from old recipes that measured ingredients by the cupful.
